newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends up on shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends up on shortcovering.

text.p: Hong Kong's spot gold ended a shade above New York's previous close on limited shortcovering, bullion dealers said on Wednesday.
The market crawled up at first, was shot down in early afternoon and then inched back up to close at US$368.80/369.30 an ounce against New York's US$368.40/80 close on Tuesday.
Traders said players in a very short market were mainly covering their positions, driving gold back up marginally.
But some selling emerged, with one gold dealer reporting he heard Russia was selling gold.

"An hour ago spot gold was belted one by a seller in Europe and the price dropped about a dollar in 10 seconds," said a bullion dealer just before the market close at 4:30 p.m. (0830 GMT). "It shows how bearish things still are."
Another trader said afternoon trading had been volatile. Buying interest in silver also helped pull up spot gold prices, dealers said.
Some traders saw producer selling interest as gold approached $370 per ounce.
"This will keep gold trading within a range of about $368 to $371," said one industry source.
Physical demand slowed slightly on Wednesday, dealers said.
Local gold ended HK$6 higher at HK$3,407 a tael.
Tael gold's steady premium over spot gold narrowed slightly, but still held firm with the U.S. dollar equivalent at $369.40/90.
"If people are selling in the tael market, they will try and cover their shorts in the spot market," said a physical gold dealer.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -7.00 from -5.20 at its previous fix.
